key_insight: ECGLight proposes a compute-light way to digitize paper ECGs so they can be analyzed by AI even in low-resource settings. The framework aims to make myocardial infarction screening more accessible without relying on strong internet or heavy hardware.
problem_solved: Many remote clinics still use paper ECG printouts, which are difficult to convert into AI-ready data because existing solutions often need high computation or reliable high-speed connectivity. This leaves valuable diagnostic information trapped on physical paper.
method: Uses a lightweight framework designed for paper ECG digitization.
Focuses on enabling myocardial infarction screening with minimal computational burden.
Targets deployment in low-connectivity, resource-constrained clinical environments.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, this highlights a practical path to deploy medical AI beyond well-equipped hospitals. It shows how model and system design can be adapted to real-world constraints, improving access to decision support in underserved regions.

paper_title: ECGLight: Compute-Light Framework For Paper ECG Digitization and Myocardial Infarction Screening
paper_authors: Shreyasvi Natraj, Cyrus Achtari, Felice Gragnano, Andrea Milzi, Marco Valgimigli
